finding.title: Localize TutorGrantPreconditionError.message instead of rendering raw English in accept/decline-invite screens

evidence.quote:
message:
            'Grant ${grant.grantId} is not in a state that can be accepted '
find.textContaining('is not in a state that can be declined'),

finding.why: tutor_invite_use_cases.dart builds TutorGrantPreconditionError.message as hardcoded English embedding an internal enum's toJson() (e.g. 'Grant abc123 is not in a state that can be accepted (current state: ...)'). accept_invite_screen.dart and decline_invite_screen.dart destructure and display it verbatim via _errorMessage = message — unlike the sibling TutorGrantFailure case, which the same files explicitly map to a localized generic string with a comment citing a prior fix ('Never surface raw Firebase/gRPC codes... always map to a friendly, localized message'). A Hebrew-locale user whose invite already expired or was handled on another device — a routine, everyday race, not an edge case — sees an untranslated, internal-looking English string. The regression tests in this batch (accept_invite_screen_l1_test.dart, decline_invite_screen_l1_test.dart) assert this raw text as the expected, correct outcome, so the bug is actively pinned rather than caught.
finding.recommendation: Give TutorGrantPreconditionError a stable code/enum instead of a message (matching the EH-5 treatment already applied to TutorGrantFailure). Resolve it to an AppLocalizations string in accept_invite_screen.dart, decline_invite_screen.dart, and invite_tutor_screen.dart (all three consumers). Update the two pinned test assertions to check the localized string.
acceptance_criteria: TutorGrantPreconditionError carries a code/enum, not a pre-formatted message; tutor_invite_use_cases.dart no longer interpolates grant id/state into user-facing text
accept_invite_screen.dart and decline_invite_screen.dart resolve the code via AppLocalizations/ARB with EN+HE parity
accept_invite_screen_l1_test.dart and decline_invite_screen_l1_test.dart assert the localized string, not literal English; a Locale('he') variant confirms the Hebrew string renders
